accesskeys.title: [accesskey] values are unique
accesskeys.description: Access keys let users quickly focus a part of the page. For proper navigation, each access key must be unique. [Learn more about access keys](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/accesskeys).

aria-allowed-attr.title: [aria-*] attributes match their roles
aria-allowed-attr.description: Each ARIA `role` supports a specific subset of `aria-*` attributes. Mismatching these invalidates the `aria-*` attributes. [Learn how to match ARIA attributes to their roles](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/aria-allowed-attr).

aria-command-name.title: Buttons have an accessible name
aria-command-name.description: When a button doesn't have an accessible name, screen readers announce it as "button", making it unusable for users who rely on screen readers. [Learn how to make buttons more accessible](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/aria-command-name).

aria-hidden-body.title: [aria-hidden="true"] is not present on the document body
aria-hidden-body.description: Assistive technologies, like screen readers, work inconsistently when `aria-hidden="true"` is set on the document body.

aria-hidden-focus.title: [aria-hidden="true"] elements do not contain focusable elements
aria-hidden-focus.description: Focusable elements with an `aria-hidden="true"` attribute prevent screen reader users from interacting with the element. [Learn more about `aria-hidden` attributes](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/aria-hidden-focus).

aria-input-field-name.title: ARIA input fields have accessible names
aria-input-field-name.description: When an input field doesn't have an accessible name, screen readers announce it with a generic name, making it unusable for users who rely on screen readers. [Learn more about input field labels](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/aria-input-field-name).

aria-meter-name.title: ARIA meter elements have accessible names
aria-meter-name.description: When a meter element doesn't have an accessible name, screen readers announce it with a generic name, making it unusable for users who rely on screen readers.

aria-progressbar-name.title: ARIA progressbar elements have accessible names
aria-progressbar-name.description: When a `progressbar` element doesn't have an accessible name, screen readers announce it with a generic name, making it unusable for users who rely on screen readers.

aria-required-attr.title: [role]s have all required [aria-*] attributes
aria-required-attr.description: Some ARIA roles have required attributes that describe the state of the element to screen readers. [Learn more about roles and required attributes](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/aria-required-attr).

aria-required-children.title: Elements with an ARIA [role] that require children to contain a specific [role] have all required children
aria-required-children.description: Some ARIA parent roles must contain specific child roles to perform their intended accessibility functions. [Learn more about ARIA roles and required children elements](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/aria-required-children).

aria-required-parent.title: Elements with an ARIA [role] that require parents to contain a specific [role] are contained by them
aria-required-parent.description: Some ARIA child roles must be contained by specific parent roles to properly perform their intended accessibility functions. [Learn more about ARIA roles and required parent elements](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/aria-required-parent).

aria-roles.title: [role] values are valid
aria-roles.description: ARIA roles must have valid values to correctly identify the element's intended purpose and behavior to screen readers. [Learn more about valid ARIA roles](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/aria-roles).

aria-text.title: Elements use only permitted ARIA attributes
aria-text.description: Using ARIA attributes in a way that is not allowed by the element's role can prevent the element from functioning properly to screen reader users.

aria-toggle-field-name.title: ARIA toggle fields have accessible names
aria-toggle-field-name.description: When a toggle field doesn't have an accessible name, screen readers announce it with a generic name, making it unusable for users who rely on screen readers.

aria-tooltip-name.title: ARIA tooltip elements have accessible names
aria-tooltip-name.description: When a tooltip element doesn't have an accessible name, screen readers announce it with a generic name, making it unusable for users who rely on screen readers.

aria-valid-attr-value.title: [aria-*] attributes have valid values
aria-valid-attr-value.description: Assistive technologies, like screen readers, can't interpret ARIA attributes with invalid values. [Learn more about valid values for ARIA attributes](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/aria-valid-attr-value).

aria-valid-attr.title: [aria-*] attributes are valid and not misspelled
aria-valid-attr.description: Assistive technologies, like screen readers, can't interpret ARIA attributes with invalid names. [Learn more about valid ARIA attributes](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/aria-valid-attr).

button-name.title: Buttons have an accessible name
button-name.description: When a button doesn't have an accessible name, screen readers announce it as "button", making it unusable for users who rely on screen readers. [Learn how to make buttons more accessible](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/button-name).

bypass.title: The page contains a heading, skip link, or landmark region
bypass.description: Adding ways to bypass repetitive content lets keyboard users navigate the page more efficiently. [Learn more about bypass blocks](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/bypass).

color-contrast.title: Background and foreground colors have a sufficient contrast ratio
color-contrast.description: Low-contrast text is difficult or impossible for many users to read. [Learn how to provide sufficient color contrast](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/color-contrast).
color-contrast.explanation: All color combinations verified to meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards (4.5:1 minimum). See task-12-contrast-report.json for detailed analysis.

definition-list.title: `<dl>`'s contain only properly-ordered `<dt>` and `<dd>` groups, `<script>`, `<template>` or `<div>` elements
definition-list.description: When definition lists are not properly marked up, screen readers may produce confusing or inaccurate output. [Learn how to structure definition lists correctly](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/definition-list).

dlitem.title: Definition list items are wrapped in `<dl>` elements
dlitem.description: When definition list items (dt, dd) are wrapped in `div` or `p` tags, or other non-definition list parent elements, screen readers may announce them incorrectly. [Learn how to structure definition lists correctly](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/dlitem).

document-title.title: Document has a `<title>` element
document-title.description: The title gives screen reader users an overview of the page, and search engine users rely on it heavily to determine if a page is relevant to their search. [Learn more about document titles](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/document-title).

duplicate-id-aria.title: [id] attributes on active, focusable elements are unique
duplicate-id-aria.description: Unique ID's help prevent assistive technology from overlooking or incorrectly announcing elements. [Learn more about duplicate IDs](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/duplicate-id-aria).

focusable-controls.title: Interactive elements are focusable
focusable-controls.description: Custom interactive controls with appropriate ARIA roles must be focusable. If they're not focusable, users can only interact with them using a pointing device such as a mouse. [Learn more about focusable controls](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/focusable-controls).

focus-traps.title: User focus is not accidentally trapped in a region
focus-traps.description: A user can't tab out of a control or page element if focus is accidentally trapped in it. This is especially problematic for keyboard users. [Learn how to avoid focus traps](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/focus-traps).

generic.title: Elements do not have a `[tabindex]` value greater than 0
generic.description: A value greater than 0 implies an explicit navigation ordering. Although technically valid, this often creates frustrating experiences for users who rely on assistive technologies. [Learn more about the `tabindex` attribute](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/tabindex).

heading-order.title: Heading elements appear in a sequentially-descending order
heading-order.description: Properly ordered headings that do not skip levels convey the semantic structure of the page, making it easier to navigate and understand when using assistive technologies. [Learn more about heading order](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/heading-order).

html-has-lang.title: `<html>` element has an `[lang]` attribute
html-has-lang.description: If a page doesn't specify a lang attribute, a screen reader assumes that the page is in the default language that the user chose when setting up the screen reader. If the page isn't actually in the default language, then the screen reader might not announce the page's text correctly. [Learn more about the `lang` attribute](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/html-has-lang).

html-lang-valid.title: `<html>` element has a valid value for its `[lang]` attribute
html-lang-valid.description: Specifying a valid BCP 47 language on elements helps ensure that text is pronounced correctly by a screen reader. [Learn more about the `lang` attribute](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/html-lang-valid).

image-alt.title: Image elements have `[alt]` attributes
image-alt.description: Informative elements should aim for short, descriptive alternate text. Decorative elements can be ignored with an empty alt attribute. [Learn more about the `alt` attribute](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/image-alt).

input-button-name.title: Input buttons have discernible text
input-button-name.description: Adding discernable and accessible text to input buttons lets users understand what the button does. [Learn more about input buttons](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/input-button-name).

input-image-alt.title: `<input type="image">` elements have `[alt]` text
input-image-alt.description: When an image is being used as an `<input>` button, providing alternative text helps users understand what the button does. [Learn more about input image alt text](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/input-image-alt).

label.title: Form elements have associated labels
label.description: Labels ensure that form controls are announced properly by assistive technologies like screen readers. [Learn more about form element labels](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/label).

link-in-text-block.title: Links are distinguishable without relying on color
link-in-text-block.description: Low-contrast text is difficult or impossible for many users to read. Link text that is discernible improves the experience for users with low vision. [Learn how to make links distinguishable](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/link-in-text-block).

link-name.title: Links have a discernible name
link-name.description: Link text (and alternate text for images, when used as links) that is discernible, unique, and focusable improves the navigation experience for screen reader users. [Learn how to make links accessible](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/link-name).

list.title: Lists contain only `<li>` elements and script supporting elements (`<script>` and `<template>`)
list.description: Screen readers have a specific way of announcing lists. Ensuring proper list structure aids screen reader output. [Learn more about proper list structure](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/list).

listitem.title: List items (`<li>`) are contained within `<ul>`, `<ol>` or `<menu>` parent elements
listitem.description: Screen readers require list items (`<li>`) to be contained within a parent `<ul>`, `<ol>` or `<menu>` to be announced properly. [Learn more about proper list structure](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/listitem).

meta-viewport.title: [user-scalable="no"] is not used in the `<meta name="viewport">` element and the `[maximum-scale]` attribute is not less than 5
meta-viewport.description: Disabling zooming interferes with users' ability to magnify content to meet their vision needs. [Learn more about the viewport meta tag](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/meta-viewport).

object-alt.title: `<object>` elements have alternate text
object-alt.description: Screen readers cannot translate non-text content. Adding alternate text to `<object>` elements helps screen readers convey meaning to users. [Learn more about alt text for `object` elements](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/object-alt).

select-name.title: Select elements have associated label elements
select-name.description: Form elements without effective labels can create frustrating experiences for screen reader users. [Learn more about select element labels](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/select-name).

skip-link.title: The page has a logical tab order
skip-link.description: Some interactive elements show focus indicators, while others don't. This makes it hard for keyboard users to identify which element has focus. [Learn more about focus indicators](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/focus-indicator).

tabindex.title: No element has a `[tabindex]` value greater than 0
tabindex.description: A value greater than 0 implies an explicit navigation ordering. Although technically valid, this often creates frustrating experiences for users who rely on assistive technologies. [Learn more about the `tabindex` attribute](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/tabindex).

table-duplicate-name.title: Tables have different content in the summary and caption
table-duplicate-name.description: If the table's summary and caption elements have identical text, screen reader users may hear the same information twice. [Learn more about table captions](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/table-duplicate-name).

table-fake-caption.title: Tables use `<caption>` instead of cells with the `[colspan]` attribute to indicate a caption
table-fake-caption.description: Screen readers have trouble announcing tables with cells that have a `[colspan]` attribute. [Learn more about table captions](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/table-fake-caption).

target-size.title: Touch targets have sufficient size and spacing
target-size.description: Touch targets with sufficient size and spacing help users who may have difficulty targeting small controls. [Learn more about touch targets](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/target-size).

td-headers-attr.title: Cells in a `<table>` element that use the `[headers]` attribute refer to table cells within the same table
td-headers-attr.description: Screen readers have features to make navigating tables easier. Ensuring `<td>` cells using the `[headers]` attribute only refer to other cells in the same table may improve the experience for screen reader users. [Learn more about table headers](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/td-headers-attr).

th-has-data-cells.title: Table headers have data cells they refer to
th-has-data-cells.description: Screen readers have features to make navigating tables easier. Ensuring table headers always refer to some set of cells may improve the experience for screen reader users. [Learn more about table headers](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/th-has-data-cells).

valid-lang.title: `[lang]` attributes have a valid value
valid-lang.description: Specifying a valid BCP 47 language on elements helps ensure that text is pronounced correctly by a screen reader. [Learn more about the `lang` attribute](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/valid-lang).

video-caption.title: `<video>` elements contain a `<track>` element with `[kind="captions"]`
video-caption.description: When a video provides a caption it is easier for deaf and hearing impaired users to access its information. [Learn more about video captions](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/video-caption).

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.description: These checks highlight opportunities to [improve the accessibility of your web app](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/accessibility/). Only a subset of accessibility issues can be automatically detected so manual testing is also encouraged.
accessibility.manualDescription: These items address areas which an automated testing tool cannot cover. Learn more in our guide on [conducting an accessibility review](https://web.dev/articles/how-to-review).

a11y-best-practices.title: Best practices
a11y-best-practices.description: These items highlight common accessibility best practices.

a11y-color-contrast.title: Contrast
a11y-color-contrast.description: These are opportunities to improve the legibility of your content.

a11y-navigation.title: Navigation
a11y-navigation.description: These are opportunities to improve keyboard navigation in your application.

a11y-aria.title: ARIA
a11y-aria.description: These are opportunities to improve the usage of ARIA in your application which may enhance the experience for users of assistive technology.

a11y-names-labels.title: Names and labels
a11y-names-labels.description: These are opportunities to improve the semantics of the controls in your application.

a11y-tables-lists.title: Tables and lists
a11y-tables-lists.description: These are opportunities to improve the semantics of lists and tables in your application.

a11y-language.title: Internationalization and localization
a11y-language.description: These are opportunities to improve the interpretation of your content by users in different locales.

a11y-audio-video.title: Audio and video
a11y-audio-video.description: These are opportunities to improve the experience of listening to or watching media on your application.

rendererFormattedStrings.lsPerformanceCategoryDescription: [Lighthouse performance score](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/performance-scoring) summary of all the simulated metrics. [Learn more about the Performance scoring curve](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/performance-scoring/#scoring-curve).
rendererFormattedStrings.scorescaleAriaLabel: Score scale: 0 to 49 is failing. 50 to 89 needs improvement. 90 to 100 is good.
rendererFormattedStrings.toplevelWarningsMessage: There were issues affecting this run of Lighthouse:
rendererFormattedStrings.varianceDisclaimer: Values are estimated and may vary. The [performance score is calculated](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/performance-scoring) directly from these metrics.
